newsitem.title: USA: Tabloid agrees to return Colorado coroner photos.
newsitem.headline: Tabloid agrees to return Colorado coroner photos.

text.p: The supermarket tabloid the Globe, which published confidential photos of slain six-year-old JonBenet Ramsey, has agreed not to use any more and to return the seven leaked to it, officials said Tuesday.

"The Globe has agreed that it will not be publishing additional photographs in its possession and will return the photographs in its possession to the coroner's office," said Boulder Deputy County Attorney Madeline Mason.

Boulder officials Monday rushed to court to stop the tabloid from publishing photos in addition to those seen in its latest edition. The settlement was made with the Globe's parent, Globe Communications Inc.

The tabloid, which defended publishing the photos taken by the coroner, came under severe criticism for receiving the pictures and most stores in Colorado refused to sell the edition, saying the issue was in bad taste. The Globe could not be reached for comment on the settlement.

But in addition to the Globe, other national magazines have also paid keen attention the case, which has left the nation spellbound. JonBenet's smiling face was on the cover of "People" and Newsweek magazines.
Meanwhile the investigation into the murder of the beauty pageant winner continued. But no suspects have been named and no arrests have been made.

A spokesman for the Ramsey family said Tuesday that former FBI agent John Douglas, who helped create profiles for serial killers and was the inspiration for one of the characters in the movie "Silence of the Lambs," was hired by the family to help with the investigation.
The city said the Boulder County Crime Stoppers was coordinating a reward of up to $100,000 for information related to the homicide investigation.
The girl's body was found Dec. 26 by her father in the basement of the family's home some eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note, demanding $118,000.
